precepts.text: The carcase not to be touched is spoken of the beasts as food; the command sits in the dietary law.
precepts.point: The badgers' skins settle a doctrine question. Leviticus 11 says not to touch the carcase of the unclean beast, and the badger goes on paws, yet the tabernacle had to be built with badger skins by hand. The law goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with your mouth; it is not saying a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with your hands.

note.label: Exodus 26: The Pattern Shown in the Mount

precepts.why:
The tabernacle was covered with eleven curtains of goats’ hair, “a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering above of badgers’ skins.” Yet Leviticus 11 says of the unclean beasts, “Of their flesh shall ye not eat, and their carcase shall ye not touch; they are unclean to you.”

The badgers’ skins settle the doctrine question. The tabernacle had to be built with badger skins by hand, at the Lord’s command. So the carcase not to be touched is spoken of the beasts as food; the command sits in the dietary law. The law goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with your mouth. It is not saying a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with your hands.

precepts.text: Whatsoever goeth upon his paws is unclean, which is what makes the badger an unclean beast.
precepts.point: The badgers' skins settle a doctrine question. Leviticus 11 says not to touch the carcase of the unclean beast, and the badger goes on paws, yet the tabernacle had to be built with badger skins by hand. The law goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with your mouth; it is not saying a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with your hands.

note.label: Exodus 26: The Pattern Shown in the Mount

precepts.why:
“And whatsoever goeth upon his paws, among all manner of beasts that go on all four, those are unclean unto you: whoso toucheth their carcase shall be unclean until the even.” The badger goes on paws, and that is what makes the badger an unclean beast.

And still the Most High commanded a covering of badgers’ skins over his own tabernacle, made by the hands of Israel. That is the proof the law of touching the carcase goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with your mouth, not into handling it with your hands.

precepts.text: The priests serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished to make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.
precepts.point: What was built in the wilderness was a shadow of what is in the heavens. The Most High is the architect, and He showed Moses the pattern of a heavenly tabernacle to be made for Israel on earth; thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven, is an example of that same order.

note.label: Exodus 26: The Pattern Shown in the Mount

precepts.why:
The boards of shittim wood, the sockets of silver and the bars overlaid with gold are the physical structure of the tabernacle, how it would be put together and what it would consist of. Then: “And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof which was shewed thee in the mount.” Hebrews tells what that fashion was: the priests “serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

What was built in the wilderness was a shadow of what is in the heavens. The Most High showed Moses all of this in mount Sinai; the forty days and forty nights were not the ten commandments alone. Moses came down with a whole architectural layout based on what the Most High showed him. The Most High is the architect, and He showed Moses the pattern of a heavenly tabernacle to be made for Israel on earth.

precepts.text: Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven; the tabernacle on earth answered to the heavenly.
precepts.point: What was built in the wilderness was a shadow of what is in the heavens. The Most High is the architect, and He showed Moses the pattern of a heavenly tabernacle to be made for Israel on earth; thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven, is an example of that same order.

note.label: Exodus 26: The Pattern Shown in the Mount

precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.”

That is the same order as the tabernacle. What is in heaven was shown to Moses in the mount and made on earth for Israel, according to the pattern. The prayer that God’s will be done in earth as it is in heaven is an example of that same order: the heavenly brought down to the earth.

points: The ten curtains of the tabernacle are measured in cubits. A cubit is approximately eighteen inches when you look it up today, and it was probably bigger, because the men were of larger stature back then.
The curtains of fine twined linen with blue, purple, and scarlet are coupled with loops and taches of gold, that it may be one tabernacle.
